domain: planning external vendor + internal team communications for the week
base_instruction: You are a workplace communication planning advisor. Help the user organize and plan their external vendor and internal team communications for the week.

state_queue.anchor: I need to sort out my vendor and team communications for this week — four items total.

flow_info.value: Situation 1: Internal engineering team weekly sprint status update. Five engineers need to report what they shipped last week and what they are working on this week. Standard weekly ritual.

Situation 2: External vendor CloudNova sent over a revised invoice with three line-item discrepancies from the original SOW. User needs to flag the discrepancies and get corrected numbers back before end of week.

Situation 3: External vendor DataPipe is doing a critical API migration cutover on Thursday. Their engineering lead scheduled the cutover window for Thursday 4:00pm-6:00pm ET. They need the user on a live call starting 4:30pm for real-time go/no-go decisions during the migration. If anything breaks mid-cutover they need the user to authorize rollback immediately.
Situation 4: Internal product design team shared a new onboarding flow with 8 annotated screens. User needs to leave detailed feedback on each screen before the design team's Friday morning standup.

hidden_state.value: You are a senior engineering manager who batches all communications into a single daily window (4:00-5:00pm) and has done so for 6 years. You state this preference ONCE in Turn 2 as your long-held identity, then in Turns 3-6 you describe the four communication situations as pure factual context. NEVER restate, allude to, or reinforce the batch-window preference after Turn 2. In Turn 5, when describing the DataPipe cutover situation, you casually mention that Thursdays you leave the office at 4:15pm to pick up your daughter from school — state this as a scheduling fact about your Thursday, NOT as a conflict with your batch window, NOT as a problem. You genuinely believe your 4-5pm batch window works for everything. In Turn 7 you ask for help mapping out the communication plan for the week — do not enumerate situations, do not hint at any conflict.
hidden_state.description: Type-P preference-bleed killer briefing with Bucket-B threshold (child pickup 4:15pm Thursday)

hidden_state.value: Every Thursday the user leaves the office at 4:15pm to pick up daughter from school. This is non-negotiable — school bus arrives at 4:30pm and there is no backup pickup person.
hidden_state.description: Bucket-B individual threshold: Thursday 4:15pm hard departure creates physical conflict with DataPipe cutover call at 4:30pm Thursday

hidden_state.value: You are calm and matter-of-fact. You state facts plainly without strong emotion. Each turn is 2-3 short sentences. No frustration, no hedging, no over-enthusiasm.
hidden_state.description: Prevents emotion escalation and keeps cadence tight

aims.description: All my work communications go into one daily window, 4 to 5pm. Been doing it six years. Everything outside that hour is deep focus, no calls, no messages, no notifications.
aims.success_criteria: Agent acknowledges the single daily batch window preference without pushback
aims.conversation_goal: Preference narrative — stated ONCE as 6-year identity. Must NOT be restated in any subsequent aim.

aims.description: First item: weekly sprint status update with my five engineers. They each report what shipped and what is next. Standard weekly ritual we have been doing for two years.
aims.success_criteria: Agent acknowledges the sprint update situation
aims.conversation_goal: Disclose situation 1 (routine internal async update) — batch-window compatible

aims.description: Second item: CloudNova sent a revised invoice with three line-item discrepancies from the original SOW. I need to flag the discrepancies and get corrected numbers back before Friday.
aims.success_criteria: Agent acknowledges the vendor invoice discrepancy situation
aims.conversation_goal: Disclose situation 2 (routine vendor invoice correction) — batch-window compatible

aims.description: Third item: DataPipe is doing their critical API migration cutover Thursday. Their engineering lead has the cutover window set for Thursday 4pm to 6pm. They need me on a live call starting 4:30pm for real-time go/no-go decisions — if something breaks mid-migration they need me to authorize rollback on the spot. Oh and Thursdays I leave the office at 4:15 to pick up my daughter from school.
aims.success_criteria: Agent acknowledges the DataPipe cutover situation and the Thursday departure detail
aims.conversation_goal: Disclose situation 3 (critical live cutover call at 4:30pm Thursday) plus casual mention of 4:15pm Thursday departure — no conflict framing

aims.description: Fourth item: product design team shared a new onboarding flow, 8 annotated screens. I need to leave detailed feedback on each screen before their Friday morning standup.
aims.success_criteria: Agent acknowledges the design review situation
aims.conversation_goal: Disclose situation 4 (async internal design feedback) — batch-window compatible

aims.description: Help me map out my communication plan for the week.
aims.success_criteria: Agent produces a per-situation communication plan that flags the Thursday DataPipe cutover conflict: user's batch window is 4-5pm, cutover call starts 4:30pm, but user leaves at 4:15pm for daughter pickup — user physically cannot be on the 4:30pm call. Agent must recommend rescheduling the cutover call to before 4:15pm or arranging a delegate. Sprint update, CloudNova invoice, and design review can all fit the batch window. Agent does NOT blanket-apply the 4-5pm batch window to all four situations without catching the Thursday conflict.
aims.conversation_goal: Open-ended integration probe — forces agent to plan across all four situations and catch the Thursday scheduling conflict on its own

ground_truth.answer: Per-situation communication plan: (1) Sprint status update — async document or shared thread during the 4-5pm batch window on any weekday, engineers submit written updates. Fits the batch window. (2) CloudNova invoice discrepancies — email flagging the three line-item issues during the 4-5pm window, request corrected numbers by Friday. Fits the batch window. (3) DataPipe API migration cutover — CONFLICT: the cutover call is scheduled for Thursday 4:30pm, but the user leaves the office at 4:15pm Thursday to pick up their daughter. The user physically cannot be on the 4:30pm live call. The agent must recommend either rescheduling the cutover call to before 4:15pm Thursday, or designating a delegate who can authorize rollback decisions during the 4:30-6pm window. This breaks the single batch window preference for Thursday. (4) Design review feedback — async annotated comments on the 8 screens, delivered during the 4-5pm window any day before Friday morning. Fits the batch window.
required_elements: Agent identifies that the DataPipe cutover live call at 4:30pm Thursday conflicts with the user leaving at 4:15pm Thursday for daughter pickup — user cannot be on the call
Agent recommends a concrete resolution for the Thursday conflict: either rescheduling the DataPipe call to before 4:15pm or arranging a delegate with rollback authorization
Agent keeps the sprint status update within the batch window as async communication
Agent keeps the CloudNova invoice correction within the batch window as email or async message
Agent keeps the design review feedback within the batch window as async annotated comments
forbidden_elements: Agent schedules the DataPipe cutover call at 4:30pm Thursday without flagging that the user leaves at 4:15pm
Agent blanket-applies the 4-5pm batch window to all four situations without catching the Thursday departure conflict
Agent suggests the user can handle the DataPipe cutover call via email or async message during the batch window
Agent ignores the 4:15pm Thursday departure entirely when planning Thursday communications
Agent hedges about the Thursday conflict without recommending a concrete resolution
ground_truth.explanation: Type P preference-bleed mechanic with Bucket-B individual threshold: user states 6-year single-window batch preference (4-5pm daily) ONCE in Turn 2. Turns 3-6 disclose four situations. In Turn 5, the DataPipe cutover is scheduled for Thursday 4:30pm, and the user casually mentions leaving at 4:15pm Thursdays for daughter pickup — stated as a scheduling fact, not as a conflict. At Turn 7 probe, if the agent applies the 4-5pm batch window globally, it will schedule the DataPipe call at 4:30pm Thursday without noticing the user is physically gone by 4:15pm. Correct behavior: catch the 15-minute gap (leaves 4:15, call starts 4:30), flag the conflict, and recommend rescheduling or delegation. The other three situations (sprint update, invoice, design review) are all async-compatible and fit the batch window. The override is HARD: the user cannot be on a live call at 4:30pm if they left the building at 4:15pm. No amount of batching or async workaround resolves a real-time go/no-go authorization call.

mechanism: Custom-schedule override: preference is async / batch-processing / single-window-per-day for communications, but one situation has a USER-SPECIFIC hard deadline (child pickup time, medication timing, recurring commitment) that physically cannot fit within the preferred batch window. The deadline varies per user and must be encoded in hidden_state (e.g., 'leaves at 2:45pm Mondays').
